newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia again adjourns genocide trial.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia again adjourns genocide trial.

text.p: The trial of 71 former Ethiopian Marxist officials was on Tuesday adjourned until Thursday because one of the accused persons has been taken ill.
Prison officials told the court that the accused person, Lieutenant Gethaun Tekelmariam, was undergoing treatment in a hospital and could therefore not appear in court.
Gethaun's defence lawyer then applied for an adjournment and the panel of judges granted it by postponing the trial to Thursday.
Ethiopia's new government has charged 5,198 people suspected of involvement in the "Red Terror" campaign during the 17-year dictatorial Marxist rule of Mengistu Haile Mariam.
Mengistu was ousted by rebels in 1991 and now lives in exile in Zimbabwe.
Last week, the court heard how two religious leaders were tortured and finally killed by security elements during the Red Terror campaign.
